text:
Maya: heads-up — hitting a nasty edge with the Python SDK streaming API when an async generator is cancelled. final token/chunk never arrives and the connection stays open (socket in CLOSE_WAIT).
Sam: ugh. any repro steps? short ones please so I can try locally.
Maya: quick repro below. essentially start iterating then cancel the consumer task right after first chunk. observed on both 'sse' and 'chunked' transports but behavior slightly different.
Maya: ```py
async def reader(client):
    stream = client.chat.stream(...)
    async for chunk in stream:
        print(chunk)
        break

async def main():
    t = asyncio.create_task(reader(client))
    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    t.cancel()
    try:
        await t
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        pass
```
Maya: after cancelling I expected the SDK to close the request and flush any buffered final chunk. instead the server log shows it still awaits EOF and the client socket lingers.
Jon: can you paste the minimal server/client logs? also which SDK version?
Maya: using 0.12.3 from pip. logs (client-side):
Maya: ```
DEBUG py-sdk.stream: sending request...
INFO py-sdk.stream: received initial chunk
DEBUG py-sdk.stream: iterator cancelled -> calling aclose()
WARNING py-sdk.stream: socket not closed, waiting for server EOF
```
Maya: and server shows request still open for ~60s before timing out.
Kevin: sounds like our aclose() path doesn't await the HTTP connection close for chunked responses. Async generator finalizers need to both cancel the read loop and call an explicit drain/flush. Also possible bug in our typing: AsyncIterator.close is not awaited in some call sites.
Sam: I vaguely remember an issue where __anext__ raising CancelledError left the reader coroutine swallowing the final chunk because we only handle GeneratorExit in sync generators.
Maya: yep. I tried adding an explicit await stream.aclose() inside the except CancelledError handler and it reduced occurrences locally.
Jon: good find. two immediate actions: 1) add a regression test that cancels mid-stream and asserts connection is closed within Xs; 2) fix the aclose/cleanup to always await the HTTP response body drain for both sse and chunked.
Kevin: also audit typing for AsyncIterator[StreamChunk] usages — if callers assume unary callback signatures we might be dropping awaits. I'll own that.
Sam: I'll open a draft PR with the test + naive fix to await flush in aclose(). Maya can you paste the small patch you used locally (so Sam can copy)?
Maya: pasted gist of change inline:
Maya: ```py
async def aclose(self):
    if self._reading_task:
        self._reading_task.cancel()
        try:
            await self._reading_task
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            pass
    # ensure transport is drained/closed
    await self._resp.content.read()
    self._transport.close()
```
Maya: it is naive (reads rest of body) but prevents socket leak in tests.
Sam: perfect, I'll iterate. assign PR to Sam and Kevin for review.
ci-bot: created issue https://redwood-internal/DEVEX-4321 "py-sdk: canceling async stream can leave socket open / final chunk dropped" and linked draft PR #987.
Maya: thanks. can we also add a short note in the Python SDK changelog about improved stream cancellation semantics and a small sample showing safe cancellation pattern (call aclose/async with)?
Kevin: yes, will add changelog entry. also add a snippet recommending using `asyncio.wait_for` with aclose timeout for user apps.
Maya: :thumbsup: closing this thread — will follow PR reviews.
